name: Quadratic formula

variables.meaning: Nonzero coefficient of the squared term
Root of the quadratic equation ax² + bx + c = 0

notes: Solves a quadratic equation in one variable.
conditions: The equation is ax² + bx + c = 0 with a ≠ 0; real roots exist when b² − 4ac ≥ 0.

name: Binomial theorem
notes: Expands an integer power of a sum into terms involving powers of x and y.
conditions: n is a nonnegative integer; the expansion also applies to commuting algebraic quantities.

name: Euler's formula
notes: Connects complex exponentials with trigonometric functions.
conditions: The angle is expressed in radians.

name: Determinant of a 2 × 2 matrix
latex: \det(A) = ad - bc,\quad A = \begin{bmatrix}a & b \\ c & d\end{bmatrix}
notes: Computes the determinant, which indicates whether a square matrix is invertible.
conditions: For a 2 × 2 matrix A is invertible exactly when ad − bc ≠ 0.

name: Inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix

variables.meaning: Matrix with rows (a, b) and (c, d)

notes: Gives a closed-form inverse for a two-by-two matrix.
conditions: The determinant ad − bc must be nonzero.

name: Characteristic equation for eigenvalues

variables.meaning: Identity matrix with the same size as A

notes: Find eigenvalues by solving the characteristic polynomial det(A − λI) = 0.
conditions: A is a square matrix and I has the same dimensions; eigenvalues may be complex.

name: Power rule for differentiation
notes: Bring the exponent down as a coefficient and reduce the exponent by one.
conditions: For real n, the rule applies where xⁿ is differentiable; for noninteger n, restrict the domain as needed.

name: Chain rule
notes: Differentiate the outer function evaluated at the inner function, then multiply by the inner derivative.
conditions: The relevant functions are differentiable at the points considered.

name: Integration by parts

variables.meaning: Differentiable function selected as the first factor

notes: Transforms an integral of a product into a related integral that may be easier to evaluate.
conditions: u and v are sufficiently differentiable and the integrals exist on the interval.

name: Fundamental theorem of calculus
notes: Evaluates a definite integral using any antiderivative of the integrand.
conditions: f is continuous on [a,b] and F is an antiderivative of f on that interval.

name: Gradient of a scalar field
latex: \nabla f = \left(\frac{\partial f}{\partial x},\frac{\partial f}{\partial y},\frac{\partial f}{\partial z}\right)

variables.meaning: Vector of the field's partial derivatives

notes: The gradient points in the direction of greatest local increase and its magnitude is the maximum directional derivative.
conditions: The scalar field is differentiable at the point.

name: Divergence of a vector field
latex: \nabla\cdot\vec{F} = \frac{\partial F_x}{\partial x}+\frac{\partial F_y}{\partial y}+\frac{\partial F_z}{\partial z}

variables.meaning: Differentiable vector field with components Fₓ, Fᵧ, F_z
Scalar divergence of the vector field

notes: Measures the net outward flux density of a vector field at a point.
conditions: The vector field has differentiable components in Cartesian coordinates.

name: First-order linear differential equation

variables.meaning: Known coefficient and forcing functions in y′ + P(x)y = Q(x)
variables.unit: depends on x and y units

variables.meaning: Integration constant determined by an initial condition

notes: Solves a first-order linear ODE using an integrating factor.
conditions: The ODE is y′ + P(x)y = Q(x) on an interval where P and Q are continuous.

name: Laplace transform of a derivative

variables.unit: inverse time when t is time

notes: Converts differentiation in time into multiplication by s and an initial-value term.
conditions: f is piecewise continuous and of exponential order so its one-sided Laplace transform exists.

name: Newton–Raphson method

variables.meaning: Next estimate produced by the iteration

notes: Iteratively improves an estimate by intersecting the tangent at the current point with the x-axis.
conditions: f′(xₙ) is nonzero and the initial estimate is sufficiently close to a root for convergence.
